{'translation': 'Apple Hardware at a Glance\n', 'reason': 'Headline; concise, vivid translation.'}

{'translation': "For nearly thirty years, Jason Kottke has been one of my primary sources for interesting things on the internet (and beyond), and there are plenty of things I'm certain I would never have discovered without him.\n", 'reason': 'Natural, fluent translation in Hong Kong style.'}

{'translation': "A few days ago, he published a post linking to the 'Dimensional Drawings' section within the 'Accessories' area of Apple's developer site.\n", 'reason': 'Natural, fluent translation.'}

{'translation': 'In short, the collection contains extremely detailed technical drawings of up to 96 devices currently, including the new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as AirPods 5.\n', 'reason': 'Natural, fluent translation.'}

{'translation': 'The lineup also includes products like MacBook Neo and the Siri Remote, as well as accessories such as AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and ZEISS optical inserts for Apple Vision Pro.\n', 'reason': 'Natural, fluent translation.'}

{'translation': "Each document contains precise measurements ranging from the device's overall dimensions and curves to the buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers, and ports, along with detailed exclusion zones and instructions indicating where specific materials cannot be placed.\n", 'reason': 'Natural, fluent translation.'}

{'translation': "Although these documents are mainly intended for accessory manufacturers, anyone with even a passing interest in hardware or industrial design—or simply someone who appreciates Apple's meticulous attention to detail—will find them worth a look.\n", 'reason': 'Natural, fluent translation.'}

{'translation': "To view Apple's dimensional drawings, please follow this link. If you haven't yet followed kottke.org, be sure to start following right away.\n", 'reason': 'Natural, fluent translation.'}
